name: Raise, price and approve variations with the client
summary: Turns extra work found on an accepted job into a priced variation, queues it to the client for approval, chases it, and records it on the job. Crons read and draft; a person approves every send. On Procore (a procore block in settings instead) it only tracks change events and logs the ones open too long; the draft, client email and follow-up email steps are ServiceM8's.

covered_by.variation-trigger: intake (a job note that says variation or extra work)
covered_by.site-check: skill (photos and notes from the site)
covered_by.scope-change: draft (priced from the rate card or a template, or a proposal)
covered_by.client-approval: approval (the client approves outside ServiceM8; a person records it)
covered_by.invoice-variation: skill (a person adds the approved lines to the job for invoicing)

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: Notes on accepted jobs that say the client has extra work.

crons.name: draft
crons.summary: Price each variation from the rate card, note it on the job, queue the client email for approval.

crons.name: follow-up
crons.summary: Queue follow-ups on variations sent for approval that are due (22:00 UTC is 8 or 9 am in eastern Australia).

crons.name: change-orders
crons.summary: Read prime and commitment change orders into complete per-project snapshots. No pricing changes or sends.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads of jobs, notes, the rate card and contacts, and one internal note on the job that records the variation. Sending the variation or a follow-up is a live operation and waits for a person.

servicem8.covers: variation notes on accepted jobs, rate-card pricing, the job record note, the client email for approval, and follow-up emails

procore.covers: change events read per project and tracked; no pricing, email or write (Procore holds pricing and approval); prime and commitment change orders tracked as read-only snapshots

gaps: Procore: the workflow tracks change events and snapshots prime and commitment change orders. It reads each project's change events, records each once and logs the ones open past stale_after_days. The page read shows change items and the change event's origin but nothing on approval, so this workflow assumes pricing and approval happen in Procore and makes no rate card, client email or follow-up email. A business sets either the procore block or the ServiceM8 variation settings, not both.
Buildxact: only its sign-in is mapped (5 operations, none for jobs or variations). Its help centre covers variations on a job, so its variation and change-order endpoints are the first thing to map.

Client approval: ServiceM8 keeps no variation or change-order record and no acceptance flow, per the platform docs. The client approves by reply or signature outside the platform, and a person records it. The kit has no command for that yet, so follow-ups stop after the set count.
Invoicing an approved variation: ServiceM8 invoices sync to Xero. A person adds the approved lines to the job. No cron does this.
Site check: a skill step (photos and notes from the site). ServiceM8 has no site-inspection support in the platform docs.

Variation PDF: the Quote template prints the whole job rather than the variation alone, so the email carries the priced lines as an HTML table and no PDF is attached. A variation-only template needs checking on a live account.
The job note's related_object value 'job' is not spelled out in the ServiceM8 spec. Confirm it on a live account. Job notes are assumed to be internal; confirm the client portal does not show them.
The adapter is docs-only until a ServiceM8 trial account proves it.

Procore not confirmed on a live account: the status words a change event returns (only 'open' is shown on the page, so only 'open' counts as open), the maximum per_page, (the Procore-Company-Id header is required on the page and is sent). Prime and commitment change order pages were rendered and read on 11 Nov; reads are built, with no pricing, approval or send operations.
